content.text: This page is the operational playbook for coding agents that need to create or update Alinea content JSON directly. It focuses on deterministic rules that match Alinea core behavior and this repository's content shapes.
Edit content through the MCP server

While `alinea dev` runs, it also serves a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server next to the local dashboard. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex use it to read the schema and to create, edit, publish and delete entries through the same write path as the dashboard. Internal fields such as `_id`, `_index`, list row ids, rich text nodes, link objects and media metadata are filled in for them, so the result is always valid and an open dashboard updates live. Prefer it over editing JSON files by hand, the rules further down this page remain the reference for manual edits.

The MCP server only exists during `alinea dev`: it is not part of `alinea build` or your deployed handler, and it only accepts requests from localhost. Its url is printed when the dev server starts (`MCP server: http://localhost:4500/mcp`), the port moves to 4501 and up when 4500 is taken.
Setup
Add the server to Claude Code:

body.code: claude mcp add --transport http alinea http://localhost:4500/mcp

content.text: Or share it with your team in a project `.mcp.json` file:
Cursor reads the same configuration from `.cursor/mcp.json`, where the `url` alone is enough. Start `alinea dev` (or your dev script that runs it) before the agent connects.
Tools

`describe_schema`: workspaces, roots, locales, types, fields and how to write a value for every field kind. Agents start with `detail: "summary"` for an overview, then describe each type they will write by passing `type`.
`find_entries`: list entries by workspace, root, type, parent, locale, status or search terms, in the order of the content tree.
`get_entry`: read an entry by id or url, rich text is returned as Markdown. Without a locale it returns the root's default locale and lists the other translations.
`create_entry`: create an entry, or a translation with `translationOf`. Rich text accepts Markdown, links accept entry ids and list rows need no ids.

`update_entry`: change some fields of an entry, published or as a draft. Only what is passed changes: object fields merge, list rows with the `_id` of an existing row merge into that row, and a list can be patched with operations instead of being sent again.
`find_references`: list the entries linking to an entry, with the field holding each link, and the entries it links to.

`delete_entry`, `publish_entry`, `archive_entry` and `move_entry`: remove entries, change their status or move them in the content tree. `delete_entry` refuses to delete an entry that other entries link to unless `force: true` is passed.

`upload_file`: add a local file or a downloaded url to the media library, with its alt text and focus point, image dimensions and previews computed. It returns the id to use in image and file fields. Pass `replace` with the id of a media entry to swap its file: the entry keeps its id, so every link to it keeps working, and the old file is removed.
List operations change rows by their `_id` and leave the others as they are:

Entries are published by default, pass `publish: false` to save a draft when drafts are enabled. Validation errors name the field path and the expected value, so the agent can correct its input and retry.
Scope and source priority
When documenting or generating Alinea content, use source of truth in this order:
The Alinea full-llms.txt file holds all documentation (including this playbook section). Use this as primary source of truth.
In case of ambiguity or missing documentation, consult the alinea core source code.
Projects using alinea will typically have alinea as a bundled node_modules dependency, which means the (compiled) source code can be accessed directly.
In case the source code can not be retrieved, or the compiled code is unclear, consult the source code on https://github.com/alineacms/alinea

Consult schema implementations and concrete JSON fixtures/content in the target project (for example `content/main/**`, `content/demo/**`) to find helpful examples and try to following the same structure when suggesting changes.

The source code of the alinea documentation website is also publicly available on https://github.com/alineacms/alineacms.com. The documentation website is itself created with Alinea + Next.js and can serve as a useful example.
Project structure conventions
In new Next.js projects, agents should follow the tutorial file structure as closely as possible to keep the codebase readable and maintainable.
In existing codebases, first scan the current structure and then align new files and changes to the established coding guidelines and architectural principles.
Entry metadata rules
Top-level entries are JSON records with required meta fields. In Alinea core this is defined by `EntryMeta` in `src/core/EntryRecord.ts`.
`_id`: unique entry id from `createId()` (`alinea/core/Id`).
`_type`: exact schema type key.
`_index`: fractional ordering key. Generate with `generateKeyBetween` from `alinea/core/util/FractionalIndexing`.
`_root`: required for root-level entries (entries without a parent). Value is the workspace root key, for example `pages` or `media`.
`_seeded`: only for entries that correspond to seeded config pages (`Config.page(...)`). Keep path stable.
ID and index generation

body.code:
# New id
node --input-type=module -e "import {createId} from 'alinea/core/Id'; console.log(createId())"

# Index between two siblings
node --input-type=module -e "import {generateKeyBetween} from 'alinea/core/util/FractionalIndexing'; console.log(generateKeyBetween('a0', 'a1'))"

# Append after last sibling
node --input-type=module -e "import {generateKeyBetween} from 'alinea/core/util/FractionalIndexing'; console.log(generateKeyBetween('a0', null))"

content.text: Alinea sorts sibling entries by `_index` ascending. Never hand-pick `_index` by eye when inserting between entries.
Internal and external links
Links appear in two places: rich text marks and link fields (`Field.link` / `Field.link.multiple`).
Rich text link marks
Rich text link mark shape is defined by `LinkMark` in `src/core/TextDoc.ts`: `_type: link`, `_id`, `_link` (`entry` | `file` | `url`), and optional `_entry`.
Link field objects
For `Field.link.multiple`, each row is also a list row, so `_index` is required.
Lists and union/list row metadata
List rows are defined by `ListRow` in `src/core/shape/ListShape.ts`. Every row must include `_id`, `_type`, `_index`.
Union values (from `UnionShape`) require `_id` and `_type`. If a union is inside a list, it still needs list row `_index` as well.
Rich text JSON format

Alinea rich text is a `TextDoc` array (`src/core/TextDoc.ts`). Common internal nodes used by this project include `heading`, `paragraph`, `text`, `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `listItem`, `hardBreak`, and block nodes like `CodeBlock`/`ImageBlock` with `_id`.

If generating from HTML, Alinea's parser maps common tags to these node/mark types (`src/core/field/RichTextField.ts`), for example `

` -> `paragraph`, `` -> `link`, `

    /
      /
    1. ` -> list nodes, `` -> `bold`.
Roots and workspaces
`Config.workspace` and `Config.root` define where content is stored and which root key each entry belongs to (`src/core/Workspace.ts`, `src/core/Root.ts`).

body.code:
// Example workspace layout in this repository
content/
  main/
    pages/
      docs.json
      docs/
        reference/
          cli.json
    media/
      screenshot.json
  demo/
    pages/
      index.json
      recipes/
        chocolate-chip.json
    media/
      ...

// Workspace key -> source
main -> content/main
demo -> content/demo

// Root key -> folder under each workspace source
pages -> <workspace>/pages
media -> <workspace>/media

content.text: Manual generation rules:
When creating a root-level entry file, include `_root` with the matching root key.
Place files under the workspace source directory and root directory that match config.
For seeded pages, keep `_seeded` stable and matching the configured seed path.
Do not remove nested identity fields (`_id`, `_index`, `_type`) from list rows, union values, or rich text block nodes.
Validation workflow

body.code:
# Normalize metadata via Alinea fix path
alinea build --fix

# In this repository
bun run build -- --fix

# Final validation
bun run build

content.text: Before commit: ensure JSON parses, `_type` matches schema, `_index` order is correct among siblings, and no duplicate `_id` values were introduced in edited scope.
